## Overview

Add opt-in sharing of DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash's immutable Engram tables across independently launched vLLM instances. One CUDA HOST_NUMA owner exports FABRIC handles; P and D import read-only GPU views and use the existing Engram gather. P/D KV transfer remains on its own connector. Implements the storage seam in [RFC #64002](https://github.com/vllm-project/vllm/issues/64002).

## Summary

```text
ASIS
P TP2 instance --> host Engram tables A (188.833 GiB)
D TP2 instance --> host Engram tables B (188.833 GiB)
```

```text
PR
one persistent owner --> P TP2: imported read-only GPU views --> Engram gather
(188.833 GiB)        +-> D TP2: imported read-only GPU views --> Engram gather
```

The measured table extent for two instances changes from 377.666 to 188.833 GiB, saving one complete table backing. This is table capacity, not total RSS, page cache or HBM.

## Claims

- Workers validate an immutable generation, checkpoint config/index hashes, FP8/E8M0 layout and table extent before importing FABRIC handles. The owner retains backing until every mapping detaches; a lost control connection becomes an uncertain lease.
- Consumers skip the two large table tensors before safetensors `get_tensor`, including mixed shards, while loading the smaller weights normally. In-place reload and weight transfer reject external Engram because a new checkpoint needs a new owner generation.
- The [runnable owner/P/D example](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/e50524f1ecaea17028a7ec82e9d8e5e0ba4498ea/examples/disaggregated/shared_engram) and [SGLang consumer example](https://github.com/foraxe/sglang/tree/cf1b37ee058b96611faee9a3879e5ee7f1baebe5/examples/engram_shared) use the same owner protocol. Each engine keeps its own KV-transfer path.

## Validation

Source head `e50524f1ecaea17028a7ec82e9d8e5e0ba4498ea`, including pinned main `6b3488cc97eed1f3b0414d84699e95c686723ebb`. The isolated GB200 runtime uses Torch 2.14.0+cu130 and older precompiled vLLM native binaries from `40fe396b`; this PR changes no native extension. Model config/index SHA256 and exact commands are in the evidence.

| Gate | Result | Scope |
| --- | --- | --- |
| Model answer, ordinary vs shared TP2 | Same 32 saved five-shot GSM8K questions: 31/32 correct in both, zero truncations, 32/32 extracted answers matched; full token streams matched 8/32. Owner 4/4 normal detaches. [Evidence](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/31b4a59d17b2691e5c4ab3310599019287ecd040/evidence/shared_engram_nvl72/merge_ready_20261103). | Captured at preceding `b4f4a8120` head. Answer-level, one local arm order; no broad quality or speed claim. |
| Final-head multimodal wrapper | Image input disabled; two 32-token text outputs, 4/4 normal detaches, owner exit zero. [Evidence](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/9e1186210df05ae93bca32797e8830334e78eb44/evidence/shared_engram_nvl72/merge_ready_followup_20261103). | Covers the subsequent LoRA-specific main merge and external checkpoint filter; no image-request claim. |
| P/D serving and cross-engine owner | One four-GB200 owner generation served vLLM and SGLang P TP2+D TP2 sequentially; both completed routed 32-token requests. A separate SGLang rerun with launcher-PID shutdown drained 8/8 leases. [Evidence](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/a29e4b6c0c511bb11915b8522eecda7e4b687410/evidence/shared_engram_nvl72/launch_close_loop_20261103). | Same host, independent engine KV transfer. A full process-group signal caused uncertain leases in the diagnostic run and is excluded from the clean-lifecycle claim. |
| Focused tests and lint | `pytest tests/models/test_deepseek_v41_shared_engram.py`, the mixed-shard loader case, `pytest tests/test_config.py -k engram`, and direct-reload compatibility cases passed on the final head (25 focused selected cases plus 48 config cases). All applicable pre-commit hooks and upstream pre-commit passed. The new direct-reload case failed on the prior branch (`DID NOT RAISE`) and passed after the guard. | CPU and local GPU evidence; upstream model CI remains separate. |

Earlier same-host component gates checked real checkpoint boundary rows, changed-ID CUDA Graph replay and TP1/TP2/TP4 table views. The prior 8K/128K/512K/1M/C128 screens are [archived with their exact older source](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/0c5abb0959234d4fd6c9e306542ddc393facc65c/evidence/shared_engram_nvl72). They do not show a stable storage-mode speedup; scheduling-budget gains are independent of this source change.

### Pinned-baseline VMM port gate

The [VMM-only port evidence](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/tree/2d2a091119c5cbe8c6b00f56b2ae8999845b01ac/evidence/shared_engram_nvl72/vmm_port_20261103) covers vLLM candidate `91816168b`
from pinned main `6b3488cc97ee` and SGLang candidate `e12dfd242`
from pinned main `99fd01047d67`. Their Git trees are exactly equal to these
existing PR heads (`e50524f1e`, `cf1b37ee`) while retaining PR ancestry.
Owner/mapping code moved to `vllm.distributed.engram_share.vmm`; no RDMA files
are in either branch. On one four-GB200 host, vLLM and SGLang each completed
P TP2+D TP2 NIXL serving with a VMM owner and eight normal detaches.
vLLM also matched seven real checkpoint boundary rows in each layer and
changed-ID graph replay, then ran a full-model TP2 decode graph with two
32-token outputs and four normal detaches. The isolated test runtime reused
older wheel assets; this is not a clean-install or cross-host gate.

## Details

- This differs from merged #62359, which shares HOST_NUMA cuMem inside one DP group: this PR gives an owner an independent lifetime and lets separate DP1 P and D instances attach. #57023 uses Mooncake ranged reads into local buffers; here the Engram kernel reads the mapped owner backing directly.
- Usage, trust boundary, generation handoff and PID-only shutdown are in [the feature guide](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/blob/e50524f1ecaea17028a7ec82e9d8e5e0ba4498ea/docs/features/engram_shared_host.md). The TCP control channel is unencrypted and requires a trusted network and private token file. The owner must not free an uncertain lease until the consumer GPU context is known gone.
- Only one four-GPU GB200 host was available. Cross-host NVL72/IMEX import, remote Grace read latency, active-graph owner failure, image-bearing requests and production SLOs remain unqualified. The [two-host gate](https://github.com/foraxe/vllm/blob/0c5abb0959234d4fd6c9e306542ddc393facc65c/evidence/shared_engram_nvl72/TWO_HOST_VALIDATION.md) is ready when a second host is available.
- AI assistance was used for source analysis, implementation, testing and this description. Human submitter line review and upstream model CI remain before merge.

@@ -0,0 +1,108 @@
+# Shared host-backed Engram tables (experimental)
+
+DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash has two immutable FP8/E8M0 Engram tables totaling
+202,758,032,400 bytes (188.833 GiB). Independently launched prefill and decode
+instances normally allocate a TP-sharded copy in each instance. This opt-in
+mode places one complete generation in a persistent owner and lets workers
+import CUDA Fabric handles. Their Engram kernels read selected rows through
+device-local virtual mappings; the row output remains in each worker's HBM.
+P/D KV transfer is configured separately.
+
+The CUDA provider uses `cuMemCreate` with `HOST_NUMA` placement and `FABRIC`
+handles. It can place chunks of one table on multiple GPU-local Grace NUMA
+nodes while mapping them as one contiguous VA in each process. Consumer GPU
+mappings request read access from the CUDA driver. Workers do not allocate,
+initialize, or load table replicas.
+
+## Scope and prerequisites
+
+- CUDA with HOST_NUMA VMM, Fabric handles, and a common NVIDIA IMEX channel for
+  owner and consumers. Cross-host use requires the same NVLink fabric domain.
+- A trusted, reachable TCP control network and the same private token file on
+  every participant. The control channel is not encrypted; use cluster network
+  isolation. FABRIC handles are accepted only by processes with IMEX access.
+- A local DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash safetensors checkpoint directory on the owner and
+  consumers. Consumers need the mixed shards for their small Engram projection
+  weights, but the two large table tensors are skipped before `get_tensor`.
+- Identical `config.json` and `model.safetensors.index.json` bytes across owner
+  and consumers. The owner records SHA256 of both table tensors; consumers
+  validate the config/index hashes, layout, encoding and explicit generation.
+  Config/index hashes do not independently verify all checkpoint weight bytes.
+- DP size 1 within each serving instance, CPU Engram offload, and explicit lazy
+  safetensors loading. TP can differ between independent instances, subject to
+  the usual model and KV connector limits.
+- In-place weight reload and weight transfer are unsupported: a new checkpoint
+  cannot change the owner's immutable Engram generation in place. Start a new
+  owner generation and new consumers for an updated checkpoint.
+
+## Start the owner
+
+The complete single-host P TP2 + D TP2 NIXL example, including owner,
+consumer launch commands and a routed request, is in
+`examples/disaggregated/shared_engram/`. SGLang consumers can use the same
+provider with their own launch recipe in
+[SGLang's VMM port](https://github.com/foraxe/sglang/tree/nyx/engram-vmm-port-99fd0104)
+(intended for [SGLang #47478](https://github.com/sgl-project/sglang/pull/47478)). The two
+engines use separate KV-transfer paths; the shared contract is the Engram
+owner generation and FABRIC handles.
+
+Create a private random token file, then start the owner on a host whose GPUs
+can access both Grace NUMA nodes. Keep it running while workers use its
+generation. The owner prints `ENGRAM_OWNER_READY` after both real tables and
+their SHA256 digests are complete.
+
+```bash
+umask 077
+openssl rand -hex 32 > /shared/private/engram.token
+python -m vllm.distributed.engram_share.vmm.owner \
+  --model-dir /models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash \
+  --listen-host OWNER_ADDRESS --listen-port 56000 \
+  --token-file /shared/private/engram.token --device 0
+```
+
+The ready line contains a generation ID. Give that ID, the owner address, and
+access to the token file to each independent worker. For example, add these
+settings to otherwise normal `vllm serve` arguments:
+
+```bash
+--engram-config '{"cpu_offload":true,"shared_host_endpoint":"OWNER_ADDRESS:56000","shared_host_token_file":"/shared/private/engram.token","shared_host_generation":"GENERATION_ID"}' \
+--load-format safetensors --safetensors-load-strategy lazy
+```
+
+The owner exchanges mapping handles at startup. It does not serve row requests.
+Workers use their own TP head ranges and existing Engram lookup/dequantization
+kernel. The backend does not depend on a vLLM DP process group or Mooncake
+Store Put/Get.
+
+## Lifetime and failure behavior
+
+Workers retain imported mappings through CUDA Graph use. During normal worker
+shutdown, vLLM first stops model execution and synchronizes the device, then
+releases mappings and owner leases. For serving, set a nonzero
+`--shutdown-timeout` so the engine drains rather than force-killing its workers.
+The owner stops accepting new attachments during shutdown and waits for all
+leases to detach. A lost control socket leaves an uncertain lease: the owner
+does not infer that GPU reads stopped, and it does not transparently fail over
+to another generation. An operator must establish that those consumer
+processes are gone before forcing owner teardown. The owner logs attach and
+detach events with a bounded client identity (host, PID, device, layer). On
+shutdown, `ENGRAM_OWNER_DRAIN_WAIT` reports active and uncertain lease IDs and
+their recorded clients every 60 seconds until all leases are released. An
+uncertain lease is not cleared automatically by a lost TCP connection.
+
+## Validation status
+
+The VMM-only port from pinned main `6b3488cc97ee` passed local four-GB200
+validation with Torch 2.14 and an older precompiled native wheel: a separate
+consumer matched seven real checkpoint boundary rows per layer and changed-ID
+CUDA Graph replay; the full TP2 model captured decode graphs at batches 1 and
+2 and generated two 32-token outputs; and P TP2 to D TP2 NIXL serving
+completed with one owner and eight normal detaches. The SGLang VMM port also
+completed its independent P/D route against this owner. These are same-host
+correctness gates, not a stable speedup or cross-host NVL72 claim.
+
+Cross-host import and serving on two NVL72 hosts have not been run because only
+one host is available. The local result establishes the mechanism and
+single-node serving behavior, not NVL72 reachability. Active-graph owner loss,
+sleep/reload, non-FP8 table encodings, and production SLO acceptance remain
+unqualified.

@@ -0,0 +1,36 @@
+# Shared Engram owner with vLLM P/D
+
+This is the tested single-host four-GPU launch shape for
+[shared host-backed Engram](../../../docs/features/engram_shared_host.md).
+The owner holds one immutable DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash table generation; two TP2
+workers import it. NIXL moves P/D KV separately. Use the same checkpoint
+directory on all three processes.
+
+```bash
+export MODEL_DIR=/models/DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash
+export TOKEN_FILE=/shared/private/engram.token
+export OWNER_ENDPOINT=127.0.0.1:56000
+export VLLM_PYTHON=/path/to/vllm/.venv/bin/python
+umask 077
+mkdir -p "$(dirname "$TOKEN_FILE")"
+openssl rand -hex 32 > "$TOKEN_FILE"
+```
+
+In terminal 1, run `./launch.sh owner`. Wait for `ENGRAM_OWNER_READY` and copy
+the `generation=` value. In terminals 2 and 3, export that value as
+`GENERATION` along with the three variables above, then run
+`./launch.sh prefill` and `./launch.sh decode`. Once both API servers are
+ready, run:
+
+```bash
+"$VLLM_PYTHON" request.py
+```
+
+Stop each server by signalling its launcher PID, then stop the owner. The owner
+waits for every lease to detach;
+if a worker loses control without detaching, verify its GPU context is gone
+before forcing owner termination. The example uses GPUs 0/1 for P and 2/3
+for D. Override `P_GPUS`, `D_GPUS`, ports, and `VLLM_PYTHON` as needed. For
+cross-host use, set a routable `OWNER_ENDPOINT` and `OWNER_BIND_HOST`, share
+the token file securely, and keep all processes in one working IMEX/NVLink
+domain. Cross-host serving has not been validated by this PR.

@@ -0,0 +1,76 @@
+#!/usr/bin/env bash
+# One owner and independent vLLM P TP2 / D TP2 workers on four local GPUs.
+set -euo pipefail
+
+role=${1:?usage: launch.sh owner|prefill|decode}
+: "${MODEL_DIR:?set MODEL_DIR to the local DeepSeek-V4.1-Flash checkpoint}"
+: "${TOKEN_FILE:?set TOKEN_FILE to a private token file shared with consumers}"
+

+"""Send one manual NIXL prefill-to-decode request to the launch.sh workers."""
+
+import argparse
+import json
+from urllib.request import Request, urlopen
+
+
+def post(url: str, payload: dict) -> dict:
+    request = Request(
+        url,
+        data=json.dumps(payload).encode(),
+        headers={"Content-Type": "application/json"},
+    )
+    with urlopen(request, timeout=600) as response:
+        return json.load(response)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser()
+    parser.add_argument("--prefill-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8100")
+    parser.add_argument("--decode-url", default="http://127.0.0.1:8200")
+    parser.add_argument("--model", default="deepseek-v41-shared")
+    parser.add_argument(
+        "--prompt", default="Explain why a CUDA graph needs stable addresses."
+    )
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    payload = {
+        "model": args.model,
+        "prompt": args.prompt,
+        "max_tokens": 1,
+        "temperature": 0,
+        "kv_transfer_params": {
+            "do_remote_decode": True,
+            "do_remote_prefill": False,
+            "remote_engine_id": None,
+            "remote_block_ids": None,
+            "remote_host": None,
+            "remote_port": None,
+        },
+    }
+    prefill = post(f"{args.prefill_url}/v1/completions", payload)
+    transfer = prefill.get("kv_transfer_params")
+    if not transfer:
+        raise RuntimeError("prefill did not return KV transfer parameters")
+    decode = post(
+        f"{args.decode_url}/v1/completions",
+        {**payload, "max_tokens": 32, "kv_transfer_params": transfer},
+    )
+    usage = decode.get("usage") or {}
+    if usage.get("completion_tokens") != 32:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"expected 32 output tokens, got {usage}")
+    choice = decode["choices"][0]
+    print(choice["text"])
+    print(
+        json.dumps(
+            {
+                "usage": usage,
+                "finish_reason": choice.get("finish_reason"),
+            }
+        )
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()

+"""CUDA VMM mappings for immutable Engram tables in HOST_NUMA memory.
+
+FABRIC handles can be sent to processes on another host in the same IMEX and
+NVLink domain. The exporter has a CPU mapping for checkpoint loading; an
+importer only maps its local GPU. Neither role depends on a vLLM process group.
+"""
+
+import ctypes
+import math
+from dataclasses import dataclass
+from types import SimpleNamespace
+
+import torch
+from cuda.bindings import driver as cu
+
+from vllm.utils.cpu_resource_utils import get_memory_node_info
+from vllm.utils.math_utils import round_up
+
+FABRIC_HANDLE = cu.CUmemAllocationHandleType.CU_MEM_HANDLE_TYPE_FABRIC
+CHUNK_BYTES = 2 << 30
+NUMA_RESERVE_FRACTION = 0.05
+
+
+class IncompleteTableMapCleanup(RuntimeError):
+    """A failed import may still have live mappings to owner backing."""
+
+
+def _call(fn, *args):
+    error, *result = fn(*args)
+    if error != cu.CUresult.CUDA_SUCCESS:
+        raise RuntimeError(f"{fn.__name__} failed: {error.name}")
+    return result[0] if result else None
+
+
+def _ranges(size: int, chunk_bytes: int = CHUNK_BYTES) -> list[tuple[int, int]]:
+    return [
+        (offset, min(chunk_bytes, size - offset))
+        for offset in range(0, size, chunk_bytes)
+    ]
+
+
+def _node_free_bytes(numa_node: int) -> int:
+    """Use physically free pages for admission; cuMemCreate may not reclaim cache."""
+    with open(f"/sys/devices/system/node/node{numa_node}/meminfo") as source:
+        for line in source:
+            parts = line.split()
+            if len(parts) >= 5 and parts[2] == "MemFree:":
+                return int(parts[3]) * 1024
+    raise RuntimeError(f"cannot read MemFree for NUMA node {numa_node}")
+
+
+def gpu_host_numa_nodes() -> tuple[int, ...]:
+    """GPU-local HOST_NUMA nodes visible to this owner process."""
+    nodes = tuple(
+        dict.fromkeys(
+            _call(
+                cu.cuDeviceGetAttribute,
+                cu.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_NUMA_ID,
+                device,
+            )
+            for device in range(torch.accelerator.device_count())
+        )
+    )
+    if not nodes:
+        raise RuntimeError("no GPU-local HOST_NUMA nodes are visible")
+    return nodes
+
+
+def _allocation_prop(numa_node: int) -> cu.CUmemAllocationProp:
+    prop = cu.CUmemAllocationProp()
+    prop.type = cu.CUmemAllocationType.CU_MEM_ALLOCATION_TYPE_PINNED
+    prop.location.type = cu.CUmemLocationType.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA
+    prop.location.id = numa_node
+    prop.requestedHandleTypes = FABRIC_HANDLE
+    return prop
+
+
+def _access(location_type, location_id: int, *, writable: bool) -> cu.CUmemAccessDesc:
+    desc = cu.CUmemAccessDesc()
+    desc.location.type = location_type
+    desc.location.id = location_id
+    desc.flags = (
+        cu.CUmemAccess_flags.CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_READWRITE
+        if writable
+        else cu.CUmemAccess_flags.CU_MEM_ACCESS_FLAGS_PROT_READ
+    )
+    return desc
+
+
+@dataclass(frozen=True)
+class TableHandles:
+    """Serializable metadata for one physical table allocation."""
+
+    size_bytes: int
+    padded_bytes: int
+    numa_node: int
+    fabric_handles: tuple[bytes, ...]
+    chunk_bytes: int = CHUNK_BYTES
+    chunk_numa_nodes: tuple[int, ...] = ()
+
+    @property
+    def placement(self) -> tuple[int, ...]:
+        return self.chunk_numa_nodes or (self.numa_node,) * len(self.fabric_handles)
+
+    def to_wire(self) -> dict:
+        return {
+            "size_bytes": self.size_bytes,
+            "padded_bytes": self.padded_bytes,
+            "numa_node": self.numa_node,
+            "chunk_bytes": self.chunk_bytes,
+            "chunk_numa_nodes": self.chunk_numa_nodes,
+            "fabric_handles": [handle.hex() for handle in self.fabric_handles],
+        }
+
+    @classmethod
+    def from_wire(cls, value: dict) -> "TableHandles":
+        size = int(value["size_bytes"])
+        padded = int(value["padded_bytes"])
+        handles = tuple(bytes.fromhex(item) for item in value["fabric_handles"])
+        chunk_bytes = int(value.get("chunk_bytes", CHUNK_BYTES))
+        nodes = tuple(int(node) for node in value.get("chunk_numa_nodes", ()))
+        if (
+            size <= 0
+            or padded < size
+            or chunk_bytes <= 0
+            or len(handles) != len(_ranges(padded, chunk_bytes))
+            or any(len(handle) != 64 for handle in handles)
+            or (nodes and len(nodes) != len(handles))
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("invalid shared Engram table extent")
+        return cls(size, padded, int(value["numa_node"]), handles, chunk_bytes, nodes)
+
+
+class TableMapping:
+    """Keep one local VA mapping alive while its tensors or graphs may use it."""
+
+    def __init__(
+        self,
+        address: int,
+        table: TableHandles,
+        mapped: list[tuple[int, int]],
+        device: int,
+        *,
+        cpu_access: bool,
+    ) -> None:
+        self.address = address
+        self.table = table
+        self._mapped = mapped
+        self.device = device
+        self._closed = False
+        self.cpu = None
+        if cpu_access:
+            self._cpu_buffer = (ctypes.c_uint8 * table.size_bytes).from_address(address)
+            self.cpu = torch.frombuffer(self._cpu_buffer, dtype=torch.uint8)
+        # The local VA is stable for the entire mapping lifetime. Tensor objects
+        # alone must never be used as an ownership or graph-quiescence signal.
+        self.cuda = torch.as_tensor(
+            SimpleNamespace(
+                __cuda_array_interface__={
+                    "shape": (table.size_bytes,),
+                    "typestr": "|u1",
+                    # PyTorch's CUDA-array importer rejects the read-only bit.
+                    # The imported VA itself has driver-level read access only.
+                    "data": (address, False),
+                    "version": 3,
+                },
+                owner=self,
+            ),
+            device=torch.device("cuda", device),
+        )
+
+    def close(self) -> None:
+        """Release only after all local GPU work, including graphs, has stopped."""
+        if self._closed:
+            return
+        try:
+            torch.accelerator.synchronize(self.device)
+        except Exception:
+            # Retain a potentially live mapping rather than invalidating it.
+            raise RuntimeError("cannot quiesce shared Engram CUDA mapping") from None
+        while self._mapped:
+            offset, length = self._mapped[-1]
+            _call(cu.cuMemUnmap, self.address + offset, length)
+            self._mapped.pop()
+        _call(cu.cuMemAddressFree, self.address, self.table.padded_bytes)
+        self._closed = True
+
+
+def _map(
+    table: TableHandles,
+    handles: list,
+    device: int,
+    *,
+    cpu_access: bool,
+) -> TableMapping:
+    if len(handles) != len(_ranges(table.padded_bytes, table.chunk_bytes)):
+        raise ValueError("shared Engram VMM handle count mismatch")
+    address = None
+    mapped: list[tuple[int, int]] = []
+    try:
+        address = int(_call(cu.cuMemAddressReserve, table.padded_bytes, 0, 0, 0))
+        for (offset, length), handle, numa_node in zip(
+            _ranges(table.padded_bytes, table.chunk_bytes),
+            handles,
+            table.placement,
+        ):
+            _call(cu.cuMemMap, address + offset, length, 0, handle, 0)
+            mapped.append((offset, length))
+            location = cu.CUmemLocationType
+            access = [
+                _access(
+                    location.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_DEVICE,
+                    device,
+                    writable=cpu_access,
+                )
+            ]
+            if cpu_access:
+                access.append(
+                    _access(
+                        location.CU_MEM_LOCATION_TYPE_HOST_NUMA,
+                        numa_node,
+                        writable=True,
+                    )
+                )
+            _call(cu.cuMemSetAccess, address + offset, length, access, len(access))
+        return TableMapping(address, table, mapped, device, cpu_access=cpu_access)
+    except BaseException as error:
+        cleanup_errors = []
+        if address is not None:
+            for offset, length in reversed(mapped):
+                try:
+                    _call(cu.cuMemUnmap, address + offset, length)
+                except Exception as exc:
+                    cleanup_errors.append(exc)
+            try:
+                _call(cu.cuMemAddressFree, address, table.padded_bytes)
+            except Exception as exc:
+                cleanup_errors.append(exc)
+        if cleanup_errors:
+            error.add_note(
+                "shared Engram map cleanup failed: "
+                + "; ".join(map(str, cleanup_errors))
+            )
+            raise IncompleteTableMapCleanup(
+                "shared Engram mapping may remain; retain the owner lease"
+            ) from error
+        raise
+
+
+def create_table(
+    size_bytes: int,
+    device: int,
+    numa_node: int | None = None,
+    *,
+    numa_nodes: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
+    chunk_bytes: int = CHUNK_BYTES,
+    chunk_placement: tuple[int, ...] | None = None,
+) -> TableMapping:
+    """Create one contiguous VA backed by FABRIC chunks on available NUMA nodes."""
+    if size_bytes <= 0:
+        raise ValueError("shared Engram table must be nonempty")
+    if numa_nodes is None:
+        if numa_node is None:
+            numa_node = _call(
+                cu.cuDeviceGetAttribute,
+                cu.CUdevice_attribute.CU_DEVICE_ATTRIBUTE_HOST_NUMA_ID,
+                device,
+            )
+        numa_nodes = (numa_node,)
+    if not numa_nodes or (numa_node is not None and numa_node not in numa_nodes):
+        raise ValueError("invalid HOST_NUMA placement")
+    props = {node: _allocation_prop(node) for node in numa_nodes}
+    granularities = {
+        node: _call(cu.cuMemGetAllocationGranularity, prop, 0)
+        for node, prop in props.items()
+    }
+    granularity = math.lcm(*granularities.values())
+    if chunk_bytes < granularity or chunk_bytes % granularity:
+        raise ValueError("shared Engram chunk must align to HOST_NUMA granularity")
+    padded = round_up(size_bytes, granularity)
+    ranges = _ranges(padded, chunk_bytes)
+    if chunk_placement is not None and len(chunk_placement) != len(ranges):
+        raise ValueError("shared Engram chunk placement length mismatch")
+    reserves = {
+        node: get_memory_node_info(node).total_memory * NUMA_RESERVE_FRACTION
+        for node in numa_nodes
+    }
+    handles = []
+    placement = []
+    try:
+        for chunk_index, (offset, length) in enumerate(ranges):
+            candidates = (
+                (chunk_placement[chunk_index],)
+                if chunk_placement is not None
+                else tuple(
+                    sorted(
+                        numa_nodes,
+                        key=lambda node: _node_free_bytes(node) - reserves[node],
+                        reverse=True,
+                    )
+                )
+            )
+            errors = []
+            for node in candidates:
+                if node not in props:
+                    raise ValueError(f"unknown HOST_NUMA node {node}")
+                free = _node_free_bytes(node)
+                if free - length < reserves[node]:
+                    errors.append(f"node {node} free {free / 2**30:.1f} GiB")
+                    continue
+                try:
+                    handle = _call(cu.cuMemCreate, length, props[node], 0)
+                except RuntimeError as exc:
+                    errors.append(f"node {node}: {exc}")
+                    continue
+                handles.append(handle)
+                placement.append(node)
+                break
+            else:
+                raise MemoryError(
+                    f"HOST_NUMA allocation failed at {offset / 2**30:.1f}/"
+                    f"{padded / 2**30:.1f} GiB: {', '.join(errors)}"
+                )
+        exported = tuple(
+            bytes(_call(cu.cuMemExportToShareableHandle, handle, FABRIC_HANDLE, 0).data)
+            for handle in handles
+        )
+        table = TableHandles(
+            size_bytes, padded, placement[0], exported, chunk_bytes, tuple(placement)
+        )
+        return _map(table, handles, device, cpu_access=True)
+    finally:
+        for handle in handles:
+            cu.cuMemRelease(handle)
+
+
+def import_table(table: TableHandles, device: int) -> TableMapping:
+    """Import on a local GPU, including when the backing is on another host."""
+    handles = []
+    try:
+        for exported in table.fabric_handles:
+            handles.append(
+                _call(cu.cuMemImportFromShareableHandle, exported, FABRIC_HANDLE)
+            )
+        return _map(table, handles, device, cpu_access=False)
+    finally:
+        for handle in handles:
+            cu.cuMemRelease(handle)

+"""Publish immutable Engram tables to independent CUDA processes.
+
+Run with ``python -m vllm.distributed.engram_share.vmm.owner``.
+The control socket only exchanges metadata and leases; lookup rows never pass
+through it. Every participant needs access to the same NVIDIA IMEX channel.
+"""
+
+import argparse
+import atexit
+import hashlib
+import json
+import logging
+import os
+import secrets
+import signal
+import socket
+import socketserver
+import threading
+from collections import Counter
+from contextlib import suppress
+from pathlib import Path
+from types import SimpleNamespace

+import torch
+from safetensors import safe_open
+
+from vllm.distributed.engram_share.vmm.mapping import (
+    IncompleteTableMapCleanup,
+    TableHandles,
+    TableMapping,
+    create_table,
+    gpu_host_numa_nodes,
+    import_table,
+)
+from vllm.models.deepseek_v41.common.engram import EngramLayout
+
+ROWS_PER_READ = 1 << 18
+MAX_CONTROL_LINE = 4096
+logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)
+_attachments: list[tuple[socket.socket, TableMapping, str]] = []
+_attachments_lock = threading.Lock()

+
+def range_chunks(table: TableHandles):
+    return (
+        (offset, min(table.chunk_bytes, table.padded_bytes - offset))
+        for offset in range(0, table.padded_bytes, table.chunk_bytes)
+    )
+
+
+def _digest_file(path: Path) -> str:
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with path.open("rb") as source:
+        while chunk := source.read(8 << 20):
+            digest.update(chunk)
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+
+
+def _checkpoint_tables(model_dir: Path) -> tuple[dict, dict]:
+    config_path = model_dir / "config.json"
+    index_path = model_dir / "model.safetensors.index.json"
+    config = json.loads(config_path.read_text())
+    text_config = config.get("text_config", config)
+    index = json.loads(index_path.read_text())["weight_map"]
+    layers = tuple(text_config["engram_layer_ids"])
+    rows = tuple(text_config["engram_num_embeddings"])
+    dim = int(text_config["engram_head_dim"])
+    if len(layers) != len(rows) or dim <= 0 or dim % 32:
+        raise ValueError("invalid Engram checkpoint layout")
+    layout = EngramLayout(SimpleNamespace(**text_config))
+    tables = {}
+    for layer_index, (layer, num_rows) in enumerate(zip(layers, rows)):
+        keys = (
+            f"layers.{layer}.engram.embed.weight",
+            f"layers.{layer}.engram.embed.scale",
+        )
+        if num_rows <= 0 or any(key not in index for key in keys):
+            raise ValueError(f"missing Engram checkpoint table for layer {layer}")
+        tables[str(layer)] = {
+            "rows": int(num_rows),
+            "dim": dim,
+            "scale_width": dim // 32,
+            "head_sizes": tuple(
+                size for order in layout.primes[layer_index] for size in order
+            ),
+            "keys": keys,
+            "files": tuple(index[key] for key in keys),
+        }
+    return {
+        "config_sha256": _digest_file(config_path),
+        "index_sha256": _digest_file(index_path),
+        "format": "FP8_E4M3FN_E8M0_BLOCK32",
+    }, tables
+
+
+def _fill_tensor(
+    destination: torch.Tensor,
+    model_dir: Path,
+    filename: str,
+    key: str,
+    rows: int,
+    width: int,
+    expected_dtype: torch.dtype,
+) -> str:
+    digest = hashlib.sha256()
+    with safe_open(model_dir / filename, framework="pt", device="cpu") as source:
+        lazy = source.get_slice(key)
+        shape = lazy.get_shape()
+        if len(shape) != 2 or shape != [rows, width]:
+            raise ValueError(f"wrong checkpoint shape for {key}: {shape}")
+        for start in range(0, rows, ROWS_PER_READ):
+            chunk = lazy[start : min(start + ROWS_PER_READ, rows)]
+            if chunk.dtype != expected_dtype:
+                raise ValueError(f"wrong checkpoint dtype for {key}: {chunk.dtype}")
+            raw = chunk.contiguous().view(torch.uint8).flatten()
+            byte_start = start * width
+            destination[byte_start : byte_start + raw.numel()].copy_(raw)
+            digest.update(raw.numpy().tobytes())
+    return digest.hexdigest()
+

+def publish_checkpoint(model_dir: Path, device: int) -> tuple[dict, list[TableMapping]]:
+    """Load full table bytes once and publish after both tensors are complete."""
+    identity, tables = _checkpoint_tables(model_dir)
+    mappings: list[TableMapping] = []
+    published = {}
+    numa_nodes = gpu_host_numa_nodes()
+    try:
+        for layer, spec in tables.items():
+            rows, dim, scale_width = (
+                spec["rows"],
+                spec["dim"],
+                spec["scale_width"],
+            )
+            weight_bytes = rows * dim
+            mapping = create_table(
+                rows * (dim + scale_width), device, numa_nodes=numa_nodes
+            )
+            mappings.append(mapping)
+            assert mapping.cpu is not None
+            weights = mapping.cpu[:weight_bytes]
+            scales = mapping.cpu[weight_bytes:]
+            weight_key, scale_key = spec["keys"]
+            weight_file, scale_file = spec["files"]
+            weight_hash = _fill_tensor(
+                weights,
+                model_dir,
+                weight_file,
+                weight_key,
+                rows,
+                dim,
+                torch.float8_e4m3fn,
+            )
+            scale_hash = _fill_tensor(
+                scales,
+                model_dir,
+                scale_file,
+                scale_key,
+                rows,
+                scale_width,
+                torch.float8_e8m0fnu,
+            )
+            published[layer] = {
+                "rows": rows,
+                "dim": dim,
+                "scale_width": scale_width,
+                "head_sizes": spec["head_sizes"],
+                "weight_sha256": weight_hash,
+                "scale_sha256": scale_hash,
+                "table": mapping.table.to_wire(),
+            }
+        torch.accelerator.synchronize(device)
+        return {
+            "schema": 1,
+            "generation": secrets.token_hex(16),
+            **identity,
+            "tables": published,
+        }, mappings
+    except BaseException:
+        for mapping in reversed(mappings):
+            mapping.close()
+        raise

+class _OwnerState:
+    def __init__(self, manifest: dict, token: str) -> None:
+        self.manifest = manifest
+        self.token = token
+        self.active: set[str] = set()
+        self.uncertain: set[str] = set()
+        self.lease_clients: dict[str, dict] = {}
+        self.draining = False
+        self.condition = threading.Condition()
+
+    def attach(self, token: str, client: dict | None = None) -> str:
+        with self.condition:
+            if self.draining or not secrets.compare_digest(token, self.token):
+                raise PermissionError("shared Engram attachment rejected")
+            lease = secrets.token_hex(16)
+            self.active.add(lease)
+            self.lease_clients[lease] = client or {}
+            print(
+                "ENGRAM_OWNER_ATTACH "
+                + json.dumps(
+                    {
+                        "generation": self.manifest["generation"],
+                        "lease": lease,
+                        "client": self.lease_clients[lease],
+                    },
+                    sort_keys=True,
+                ),
+                flush=True,
+            )
+            return lease
+
+    def detach(self, lease: str) -> None:
+        with self.condition:
+            self.active.remove(lease)
+            client = self.lease_clients.pop(lease, {})
+            print(
+                "ENGRAM_OWNER_DETACH "
+                + json.dumps(
+                    {
+                        "generation": self.manifest["generation"],
+                        "lease": lease,
+                        "client": client,
+                    },
+                    sort_keys=True,
+                ),
+                flush=True,
+            )
+            self.condition.notify_all()
+
+    def lose_control(self, lease: str) -> None:
+        with self.condition:
+            self.active.discard(lease)
+            self.uncertain.add(lease)
+            logger.warning(
+                "Engram lease control lost; retaining backing: %s client=%s",
+                lease,
+                self.lease_clients.get(lease, {}),
+            )
+            self.condition.notify_all()
+
+    def drain_status(self) -> dict:
+        """Snapshot outstanding leases while holding the condition lock."""
+        return {
+            "generation": self.manifest["generation"],
+            "active": sorted(self.active),
+            "uncertain": sorted(self.uncertain),
+            "clients": {
+                lease: self.lease_clients.get(lease, {})
+                for lease in sorted(self.active | self.uncertain)
+            },
+        }

+class _RequestHandler(socketserver.StreamRequestHandler):
+    def handle(self) -> None:
+        state: _OwnerState = self.server.owner_state  # type: ignore[attr-defined]
+        lease = None
+        try:
+            self.request.settimeout(30)
+            request = json.loads(self.rfile.readline(MAX_CONTROL_LINE))
+            if request.get("op") != "attach":
+                raise ValueError("expected attach")
+            client: dict[str, str | int] = {"peer": str(self.client_address[0])}
+            supplied = request.get("client")
+            if isinstance(supplied, dict):
+                for key in ("hostname", "pid", "device", "layer"):
+                    value = supplied.get(key)
+                    if (
+                        isinstance(value, int)
+                        and value >= 0
+                        or isinstance(value, str)
+                        and len(value) <= 128
+                    ):
+                        client[key] = value
+            lease = state.attach(str(request.get("token", "")), client)
+            reply = {"ok": True, "lease": lease, "manifest": state.manifest}
+            self.wfile.write(json.dumps(reply).encode() + b"\n")
+            self.wfile.flush()
+            self.request.settimeout(None)
+            line = self.rfile.readline(MAX_CONTROL_LINE)
+            if not line:
+                raise ConnectionError("consumer control socket closed")
+            request = json.loads(line)
+            if request != {"op": "detach", "lease": lease}:
+                raise ValueError("consumer did not detach its lease")
+            state.detach(lease)
+            lease = None
+            self.wfile.write(b'{"ok":true}\n')
+            self.wfile.flush()
+        except Exception as exc:
+            if lease is not None:
+                state.lose_control(lease)
+            try:
+                self.wfile.write(
+                    json.dumps({"ok": False, "error": str(exc)}).encode() + b"\n"
+                )
+                self.wfile.flush()
+            except OSError:
+                pass

+def run_owner(model_dir: Path, address: tuple[str, int], token_file: Path, device: int):
+    token = token_file.read_text().strip()
+    if len(token) < 32 or token_file.stat().st_mode & 0o077:
+        raise ValueError("token file must hold at least 32 private characters")

+    manifest, mappings = publish_checkpoint(model_dir, device)
+    state = _OwnerState(manifest, token)

+    for sig in (signal.SIGINT, signal.SIGTERM):
+        signal.signal(sig, lambda _sig, _frame: stop.set())

+        server = _OwnerServer(address, state)
+    except BaseException:
+        for mapping in reversed(mappings):
+            mapping.close()
+        raise

+        thread = threading.Thread(target=server.serve_forever, daemon=True)
+        thread.start()

+        for mapping in mappings:
+            for node, (_, length) in zip(
+                mapping.table.placement,
+                range_chunks(mapping.table),

+                node_bytes[node] += length

+            + json.dumps(

+                    "table_bytes": sum(
+                        mapping.table.size_bytes for mapping in mappings

+                    "padded_bytes": sum(
+                        mapping.table.padded_bytes for mapping in mappings
+                    ),
+                    "node_bytes": dict(node_bytes),
+                }
+            ),
+            flush=True,
+        )
+        bound_host = server.server_address[0]
+        host = bound_host.decode() if isinstance(bound_host, bytes) else bound_host

+            f"ENGRAM_OWNER_READY {host}:{server.server_address[1]} "
+            f"generation={manifest['generation']}",
+            flush=True,
+        )

+        with state.condition:
+            state.draining = True
+        server.shutdown()
+        thread.join()
+        with state.condition:
+            while state.active or state.uncertain:
+                print(
+                    "ENGRAM_OWNER_DRAIN_WAIT "
+                    + json.dumps(state.drain_status(), sort_keys=True),
+                    flush=True,

+                state.condition.wait(timeout=60)

+def attach_table(
+    endpoint: str,
+    token_file: Path,
+    layer: int,
+    rows: int,
+    dim: int,
+    head_sizes: tuple[int, ...],
+    device: int,
+    expected_generation: str | None = None,
+    checkpoint_dir: Path | None = None,
+) -> tuple[socket.socket, TableMapping, dict]:
+    """Attach one layer and retain the control socket as its owner lease."""
+    host, port = endpoint.rsplit(":", 1)
+    connection = socket.create_connection((host, int(port)), timeout=30)
+    lease = None
+    try:
+        token = token_file.read_text().strip()
+        request = {
+            "op": "attach",
+            "token": token,
+            "client": {
+                "hostname": socket.gethostname(),
+                "pid": os.getpid(),
+                "device": device,
+                "layer": layer,
+            },
+        }
+        connection.sendall(json.dumps(request).encode() + b"\n")
+        response = b""
+        while not response.endswith(b"\n"):
+            part = connection.recv(1 << 20)
+            if not part:
+                raise ConnectionError("Engram owner closed during attach")
+            response += part
+            if len(response) > 1 << 20:
+                raise ValueError("Engram owner manifest is too large")
+        reply = json.loads(response)
+        if not reply.get("ok"):
+            raise RuntimeError(
+                f"Engram owner rejected attachment: {reply.get('error')}"
+            )
+        lease = reply["lease"]
+        manifest = reply["manifest"]
+        if (
+            expected_generation is not None
+            and manifest["generation"] != expected_generation
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("unexpected shared Engram generation")
+        if checkpoint_dir is not None:
+            if not checkpoint_dir.is_dir():
+                raise ValueError("shared Engram needs a local checkpoint directory")
+            expected_hashes = {
+                "config_sha256": _digest_file(checkpoint_dir / "config.json"),
+                "index_sha256": _digest_file(
+                    checkpoint_dir / "model.safetensors.index.json"
+                ),
+            }
+            if any(
+                manifest.get(key) != value for key, value in expected_hashes.items()
+            ):
+                raise ValueError("shared Engram checkpoint metadata mismatch")

+        if (
+            manifest["schema"] != 1
+            or manifest["format"] != "FP8_E4M3FN_E8M0_BLOCK32"
+            or spec["rows"] != rows
+            or spec["dim"] != dim
+            or spec["scale_width"] != dim // 32
+            or tuple(spec["head_sizes"]) != head_sizes
+        ):
+            raise ValueError("Engram owner generation has incompatible table layout")
+        table = TableHandles.from_wire(spec["table"])
+        if table.size_bytes != rows * (dim + dim // 32):
+            raise ValueError("Engram owner table byte size mismatch")
+        mapping = import_table(table, device)
+        return connection, mapping, {"lease": lease, **manifest}
+    except BaseException as error:
+        if isinstance(error, IncompleteTableMapCleanup):
+            connection.close()
+            raise
+        if lease is not None:
+            with suppress(OSError):
+                connection.sendall(
+                    json.dumps({"op": "detach", "lease": lease}).encode() + b"\n"
+                )
+        connection.close()
+        raise
+
+
+def detach_table(connection: socket.socket, mapping: TableMapping, lease: str) -> None:
+    """Quiesce local work before releasing the owner's lease."""
+    mapping.close()
+    try:
+        connection.sendall(
+            json.dumps({"op": "detach", "lease": lease}).encode() + b"\n"
+        )
+    finally:
+        connection.close()
+
+
+def retain_attachment(
+    connection: socket.socket, mapping: TableMapping, lease: str
+) -> None:
+    """Keep mappings until worker shutdown has quiesced its graphs."""
+    with _attachments_lock:
+        _attachments.append((connection, mapping, lease))
+
+
+def close_attached_tables() -> None:
+    """Release all tables after the model runner stops replaying graphs."""
+    with _attachments_lock:
+        for attachment in reversed(_attachments[:]):
+            try:
+                detach_table(*attachment)
+            except Exception:
+                logger.exception("Cannot safely detach an external Engram table")
+            else:
+                _attachments.remove(attachment)
+
+
+atexit.register(close_attached_tables)
+
+
+def main() -> None:
+    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(description="Own immutable shared Engram tables")
+    parser.add_argument("--model-dir", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--listen-host", required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--listen-port", type=int, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--token-file", type=Path, required=True)
+    parser.add_argument("--device", type=int, default=0)
+    args = parser.parse_args()
+    if not args.model_dir.is_dir():
+        parser.error("--model-dir must be a local checkpoint directory")
+    if args.listen_port < 1 or args.listen_port > 65535:
+        parser.error("--listen-port must be between 1 and 65535")
+    os.umask(0o077)
+    run_owner(
+        args.model_dir,
+        (args.listen_host, args.listen_port),
+        args.token_file,
+        args.device,
+    )
+
+
+if __name__ == "__main__":
+    main()
